title: Reduction commutes with completed pullback
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, coefficient sheaves $A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$ for $W=T,T'$, and reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T))$ be derived $I$-complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$. Let $L=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T'_{\Proet},A_{T'}))$ be the completed pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and write $g_n^*$ for finite-coefficient module pullback as there.

Then $L$ is derived $I$-complete, and for every $n\geq1$ the projection of its defining derived limit to $Lg_n^*K_n$ induces a functorial isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(T'_{\Proet},(P_n)_{T'}))$,
$$\alpha_n:L\otimes^L_{A_{T'}}(P_n)_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_n^*K_n.$$
These isomorphisms commute with the quotient transition maps. For $b\geq a\geq1$ they also commute with normalization: extending $\alpha_b$ from $(P_b)_{T'}$ to $(P_a)_{T'}$ and then using the normalization of the pulled-back reduction tower gives $\alpha_a$ after the canonical scalar-extension associativity identification. For $c\geq b\geq a$ these normalizations satisfy the quotient cocycle, and for equal indices the unit identity. All tensor products in the display are over the indicated sheaves of rings; no identification with an ordinary module derived category is asserted.

proof.text: Write $R_W=\underline A_W$, $S_{n,W}=\underline{P_n}_W$ and $\operatorname{Res}_W$ for restriction from $A_W$ to $R_W$. Put $N=Lg^*_{\underline A}\operatorname{Res}_T K$ and $N_n=N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$. The constant-to-completed coefficient comparison [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and the completed-pullback construction [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] identify the restricted pulled-back strict tower with $(N_n)_n$, including quotient transitions. They identify $\operatorname{Res}_{T'}L$ with $\widehat N=R\lim_nN_n$, and the comparison from ordinary constant-coefficient pullback with its completion unit $\eta:N\to\widehat N$. In particular $p_n\eta=u_n$, where $p_n:\widehat N\to\operatorname{Res}N_n$ is evaluation and $u_n:N\to\operatorname{Res}N_n$ is the quotient unit. These are comparisons of strict towers and their evaluations, not an exchange of inverse image and infinite limits. The hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum] hold for $(T',\Lambda=A,I,N)$: Noetherianity, finite generation, additive torsion of $A/I$, and perfectness of every $P_n$ are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. No completeness of $N$ is asserted.

source.place: Second paragraph: ordinary pullback and its reduction tower; Stacks 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), (2), (5)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] on the small site $T'_{\Proet}$ with $\mathcal O=R_{T'}$ and the finite generators of $I$. For arbitrary $N$ its Koszul completion is locally derived complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] this Koszul limit, with its unit, is $\widehat N$ of step 1. Thus the Koszul completion unit of $\widehat N$ is an isomorphism, by the same reflector. Now form the Koszul completion unit of $L$ over $A_{T'}$. The restriction comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identify its restriction with the Koszul unit of $\operatorname{Res}_{T'}L=\widehat N$: the Koszul factors are finite free and restriction identifies the derived limits and units. Restriction is exact and unchanged on underlying abelian sheaves, so the cohomology sheaves of a restricted cone vanish only if those of the original cone vanish. It therefore reflects isomorphisms. The Koszul unit of $L$ is an isomorphism, which is precisely derived $I$-completeness in [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion].

Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] to $X=T'$, $\Lambda=A$, and $K=N$, with the datum verified in step 1. Its strict tower is exactly $(N_n)_n$, and it imposes no derived-completeness hypothesis on $N$. It gives a functorial isomorphism $\beta_n:\widehat N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}\to N_n$ in the quotient-coefficient derived category, specifically the scalar-extension adjoint of $p_n$. The finite comparisons and evaluation comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] identify its source with $L\otimes^L_{A_{T'}}(P_n)_{T'}$ and its target with $Lg_n^*K_n$. Because the strict tower comparison preserves $p_n$, its adjoint is the projection-induced $\alpha_n$ in the statement. Thus $\alpha_n$ is an isomorphism in the indicated quotient-coefficient category and is natural in $K$.

source.place: First paragraph, finite reduction; second paragraph, apply finite reduction of adic completion to ordinary pullback

proof.text: To verify the coherence of these specified maps, set $r_n=\eta\otimes^L1:N_n\to\widehat N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$. Use the canonical derived adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] for the identity underlying topos with ring map $R_{T'}\to S_{n,T'}$; direct image is exact restriction of scalars. The adjunct of $\beta_nr_n$ is $p_n\eta=u_n$ by step 1. The adjunct of $1_{N_n}$ is also $u_n$, so $\beta_nr_n=1_{N_n}$. Since $\beta_n$ is an isomorphism by step 3, $r_n=\beta_n^{-1}$. This is an adjunction identity, not a claim that the unreduced completion unit $\eta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Compatibility clause: identify the finite comparison as the inverse of the reduced completion unit

proof.text: Let $q^N_{b,a}$ and $q^{\widehat N}_{b,a}$ be the quotient-transition maps of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Naturality of tensoring $\eta$ with $P_b\to P_a$ gives $q^{\widehat N}_{b,a}r_b=r_aq^N_{b,a}$. Multiplying on the left by $\beta_a$ and on the right by $\beta_b$ and using step 4 yields $q^N_{b,a}\beta_b=\beta_aq^{\widehat N}_{b,a}$. The finite comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] commute with these quotient transitions; the tower in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] has the pulled-back transitions. Hence this equation is exactly the transition square for $\alpha_b,\alpha_a$.

source.place: First paragraph, compatibility with the transition maps

proof.text: Write $\theta^N_{b,a}$ and $\theta^{\widehat N}_{b,a}$ for the scalar-extension normalization maps of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Their naturality gives $\theta^{\widehat N}_{b,a}(r_b\otimes^L1)=r_a\theta^N_{b,a}$. Substitution of step 4 and cancellation gives $\theta^N_{b,a}(\beta_b\otimes^L1)=\beta_a\theta^{\widehat N}_{b,a}$. These are also the intended normalizations after the finite coefficient comparisons: the balancing maps in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] send $(x\otimes t)\otimes s$ to $x\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$. Applying inverse image and scalar extension to this formula gives the same map for the pulled-back reduction tower. This computation is valid on K-flat representatives, since [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] says pullback preserves that resolving class and identifies the derived tensor comparison. Thus the equation just proved is the required normalization square for $\alpha$. For three levels both normalization composites send $((x\otimes t)\otimes s)\otimes v$ to $x\otimes q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$; for equal indices they are the balancing unit. These sectionwise formulas respect restrictions and differentials, so give the asserted cocycle and unit equations in the derived categories. Naturality follows from the same formulas with $x$ replaced by its image under a chain map, independently of the K-flat representative.

source.place: First paragraph, normalization cocycles; coefficient normalizations computed before and after pullback

blueprint_sketch.proof:
Derived pullback commutes with derived tensor, so its defining tower is the
reduction tower of $Lg^*K$. Apply finite reduction of adic completion to
this object. Its level $n$ is
$Lg^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n\simeq Lg^*(K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n)=Lg^*K_n$.

 (Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K)\otimes_A^LP_n
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_n^*K_n,

proof.text:

[def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Tensoring the defining derived
limit with $P_n$ and using the finite reduction of
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-reduction-reconstruction] gives the displayed
isomorphism, with the stated compatibilities inherited from the tower
structure.
